entries.name: Southern live oak
entries.leaves: evergreen, small dark leathery leaves, draped with Spanish moss
entries.voxel_shape: broad spreading evergreen crown wider than the tree is tall, thick curved trunk with low limbs
entries.notes: The signature tree of the deep South: moss-hung limbs spreading flat like an umbrella. Plant one and the whole south-east corner of the map feels different.

entries.name: Southern magnolia
entries.leaves: evergreen, large glossy dark green with rusty undersides
entries.flowers: huge creamy-white, fragrant, late spring to summer
entries.fruit: cone-like aggregate with bright red seeds
entries.voxel_shape: dense pyramidal evergreen, glossy canopy, trunk straight
entries.notes: Flowers the size of dinner plates and a perfume that carries across a garden. The classic front-yard icon of the humid subtropics.

entries.name: Bald cypress
entries.leaves: deciduous, soft feathery needles turning rust-orange in autumn
entries.voxel_shape: massive fluted trunk with flared buttress base, conical crown, knees poking up around it in swamps
entries.notes: Grows straight out of water; the biggest ones dwarf everything else in the swamp and throw 'knees' above the waterline. Votes for any flooded river biome.

entries.name: Sweetgum
entries.leaves: deciduous, star-shaped with 5-7 lobes, brilliant red-purple autumn colour
entries.flowers: small greenish globular heads, spring, wind-pollinated
entries.fruit: hard spiky brown balls, hang on all winter
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight trunk, conical-oval crown, star leaves; spiky ball fruits underfoot
entries.notes: The star-leaved autumn firework; bare-branched in winter, it is the tree whose spiky balls get into every garden.

entries.name: Loblolly pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, long needles in bundles of three
entries.flowers: male pollen cones and small female cones, spring
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight column with a small high crown, planted forests read as green grid columns
entries.notes: The workhorse of southern forestry; fastest-growing pine of the US South. A planted stand is cheap, tall and uniform.

entries.name: Longleaf pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, very long needles (30-45 cm) in bundles of three
entries.flowers: male pollen cones and female cones, spring
entries.voxel_shape: straight high-canopied trunk; young trees sit as a fire-proof grass-like tuft for years
entries.notes: Spends years as a fireproof 'grass stage' tuft, then rockets up. The grass stage is a fun growth-phase mechanic to model.

entries.name: Tulip poplar
entries.leaves: deciduous, distinctive four-lobed saddle shape with a notched tip
entries.flowers: tulip-shaped, greenish-yellow with orange base, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: very tall straight pale trunk, narrow oval crown, seed cones standing upright among the leaves
entries.notes: Among the tallest eastern hardwoods; the saddle-shaped leaf and tulip flower are instantly recognisable silhouettes.

entries.name: Flowering dogwood
entries.leaves: deciduous, oval, reddish-wine autumn foliage
entries.flowers: showy white or pink bracts in spring before the leaves
entries.fruit: bright red drupes, loved by birds
entries.voxel_shape: small layered-horizontal small tree, open tiered crown, white bract display in April
entries.notes: A spring-flowering understorey tree; two waves of colour (white bracts, red fruits) make it a seasonal calendar marker.

entries.name: Water tupelo
entries.leaves: deciduous, large oval leaves, poisonous-looking gloss
entries.voxel_shape: swollen bottle-like trunk base in water, open spreading crown, standing in flooded swamp forest
entries.notes: The source of tupelo honey: beekeepers float apiaries into its swamp bloom each May. A flooded-forest specialist.

entries.name: American holly
entries.leaves: evergreen, spiny dark leaves, glossy
entries.fruit: shiny red berries on female trees, winter
entries.voxel_shape: dense pyramidal evergreen, dark, stiff spiny foliage, red berries in the winter scene
entries.notes: The Christmas holly of the eastern US; berries feed robins and cedar waxwings all winter. Sexes are separate trees.

entries.name: Pecan
entries.leaves: deciduous, pinnate compound leaves with 11-17 leaflets
entries.fruit: pecans, in thin husks that split in autumn
entries.voxel_shape: tall open tree, long oval crown, rachis leaves fluttering like willow
entries.notes: The US native nut tree; big bottomland pecan groves once lined southern rivers. Pecan pie is a gameplay use waiting to happen.

entries.name: Cabbage palmetto
entries.leaves: evergreen, large fan-shaped fronds on a single unbranched trunk
entries.voxel_shape: slim unbranched column topped by a burst of pleated fan fronds
entries.notes: Palm that shrugs off fire and hurricanes with a bendy trunk; the edge between the subtropical forest and the coast.

entries.name: Spanish moss
entries.leaves: grey-green hanging strands, absorbs water and nutrients from the air, roots on nothing
entries.voxel_shape: grey-green hair hanging from live oak limbs; pure drape, no trunk, no leaves of its own
entries.notes: Not a moss and not Spanish: a bromeliad that lives on air. Hangs from oaks and cypress; the single fastest way to sell 'deep South'.

entries.name: Resurrection fern
entries.leaves: evergreen when wet; curls into brown crisped fronds and lies dormant for drought, greening within hours of rain
entries.voxel_shape: small fronds glued flat to bark; invisible until rain turns them vivid green overnight
entries.notes: The immortal houseplant: can appear dead for decades, then unfurl after a storm. Designer hook for a 'drought that ends' moment.

entries.name: Yaupon holly
entries.leaves: evergreen, small rounded leaves, greyish bark
entries.voxel_shape: dense rounded evergreen shrub, white-boiled branches in old age
uses: caffeine tea (the only native US tea plant, Timucuan 'asi')
entries.notes: Brewed as a caffeine tea by southeastern tribes for millennia; a real 'find the tea bush' survival mechanic.

entries.name: American beautyberry
entries.leaves: deciduous, arching branches, lime-green in summer
entries.flowers: tiny pink clusters along the stems, summer
entries.fruit: electric-purple berry rings around the stems, early autumn
entries.voxel_shape: loose arching shrub, purple beaded stems in autumn that birds strip clean
entries.notes: The purple-beaded bush of autumn roadsides; the colour payoff is worth the small size of the plant.

entries.name: Tea plant
entries.leaves: evergreen, glossy, dark, young leaves picked for tea
entries.voxel_shape: low hedged bush in plantations; a big glossy camellia with the leaves plucked off the top
entries.notes: Cultivated as knee-high plucked hedges; left wild it grows into a 2 m camellia. The most-drunk brewed plant on Earth.

entries.name: Japanese camellia
entries.leaves: evergreen, glossy dark, serrated edges
entries.flowers: rose-like, red to white, late winter to spring, no scent
entries.voxel_shape: dense glossy evergreen mound, full of perfect rose flowers in the cold months
entries.notes: The winter rose: blooms when nothing else does, a splash of crimson underbare oaks. Tea plant's showier cousin.

entries.name: Japanese flowering cherry
entries.leaves: deciduous, coppery when young, green then bronze-red
entries.flowers: massed pink-white blossom, early spring, the sakura festival tree
entries.fruit: small black cherries (ornamental forms set little fruit)
entries.voxel_shape: wide vase crown; for two weeks a year it is a solid pink cloud, then bare
entries.notes: Ephemeral is the whole point: one glorious week, then petals like snow. A timing-based 'event' tree for the game.

entries.name: Japanese maple
entries.leaves: deciduous, deeply cut hand-shaped leaves, scarlet in autumn; dwarf cultivars stay small
entries.voxel_shape: small layered tree, fine-textured dome of lacy leaves, blazing red in October
entries.notes: The connoisseur's maple: lacy leaves and impossible autumn reds. Cultivars run from ground-hugging mounds to 10 m trees.

entries.name: Ginkgo
entries.leaves: deciduous, unique fan shape with a split notch, turning pure yellow in a single day
entries.flowers: small cones, spring; female trees produce fleshy seeds that smell rancid
entries.fruit: yellow fleshy seeds, foul-smelling, edible nuts inside
entries.voxel_shape: big straight grey trunk, upright branches, fan leaves; one day in November the whole tree turns yellow
entries.notes: A 200-million-year-old living fossil that shrugged off Hiroshima. Female trees smell awful; plant only males in cities.

entries.name: Camphor laurel
entries.leaves: evergreen, glossy, smell of camphor when crushed
entries.voxel_shape: huge dense dome on a massive trunk; the classic shade banyan of eastern Asia
entries.notes: Crush a leaf and the whole tree smells of Tiger Balm. Massive, sacred old specimens anchor temple courtyards.

entries.name: Moso bamboo
entries.leaves: evergreen, delicate lanceolate leaves, dense groves
entries.flowers: rare, flowering happens once every decades and then the culm dies
entries.voxel_shape: towering vertical green tubes in dense stands, sighing and rattling in the wind
entries.notes: The fastest plant that reaches tree height; a shoot can grow a metre a day. Flowers gregariously and then whole stands die.

entries.name: Sweet osmanthus
entries.leaves: evergreen, small leathery leaves with spiny edges on young plants
entries.fruit: small purple-black drupes, rare in cultivation
entries.voxel_shape: rounded dense large shrub; in October the air smells of apricot jam
entries.notes: You smell it before you see it: September in China tastes like apricot. Tiny flowers, gigantic perfume.

entries.name: Dawn redwood
entries.leaves: deciduous conifer, soft feathery needles, fresh green then russet in autumn
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight fluted trunk with fastigiate branches, like a feathery redwood
entries.notes: Known only from fossils until a living grove was found in rural China in 1941. Grows alarmingly fast from a sprig.

entries.name: Empress tree
entries.leaves: deciduous, enormous heart-shaped leaves (30-40 cm), velvety
entries.flowers: large upright panicles of violet-blue foxglove flowers in spring, before the leaves
entries.fruit: woody egg-shaped capsules full of winged seeds; a single tree releases millions
entries.voxel_shape: fast pale column with huge leaves, a shower of violet trumpets in early spring
entries.notes: Grows so fast it was planted on burial mounds at birth to carve a dowry chest at majority. Now a notorious invasive abroad.

entries.name: Tree of heaven
entries.leaves: deciduous, pinnate leaves over a metre long, smell of rancid peanuts when crushed
entries.voxel_shape: gangly straight trunk with a loose tropical fern of a crown, cracks pavement and rails
entries.notes: The immigrant's ladder tree: grows through concrete, sewers and poverty, smells terrible, feeds spotted lanternfly. Wildly invasive.

entries.name: Sacred lotus
entries.leaves: large round waxy pads held above the water on stalks, ultrahydrophobic so rain rolls off clean
entries.flowers: large pink or white, rising on stalks above the pads, summer
entries.fruit: showerhead seed pod with holes holding hard seeds (lotus seeds)
entries.voxel_shape: bowl-like leaves floating on still water, a pink candle rising out of the middle
entries.notes: Seeds have germinated after 1300 years in lake mud. Underwater rhizomes carry the whole plant; pads and flowers are theatre.

entries.name: Kudzu
entries.leaves: deciduous, huge three-part leaves, entire hillsides can vanish under it
entries.voxel_shape: a green tide rolling over bushes, power lines and barns; 30 cm of new growth per day
uses: food source (trials in the US South)
entries.notes: Planted to stop erosion, now eating the South at a steady crawl: it can bury a building in a decade. A slow-motion catastrophe you can farm.

entries.name: Chinese silvergrass
entries.leaves: deciduous, arching blade leaves with a white midrib
entries.voxel_shape: fountains of arching grass with fluffy plume tufts; glows silver in backlight
entries.notes: The fountain grass of Japanese gardens; feathery plumes in autumn light. Sterile hybrids are the safe ornamental choice.

entries.name: Jacaranda
entries.leaves: deciduous, ferny bipinnate leaves, shower of violet petals in spring before the leaves
entries.fruit: flat woody clamshells full of winged seeds
entries.voxel_shape: open crown dripping with violet; petal carpets purple under every tree for weeks
entries.notes: The November tree: Pretoria and Buenos Aires turn violet. Streets planted in jacaranda are a mandatory screenshot.

entries.name: Ombú
entries.leaves: evergreen, broad oval leaves, a spreading sea of dark canopy
entries.voxel_shape: a colossal swollen multi-trunked dome; the Pampas' one landmark for miles
entries.notes: Not woody at all: a giant herb over a swollen water-storing base. Gauchos navigated by it; one ombú can shelter a whole herd.

entries.name: Paraná pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, stiff sharp scale-leaves in spiralling whorls forming a symmetrical candelabra crown
entries.flowers: cones, spring; huge male and female cones on different trees
entries.fruit: large cones dropping heavy pine nuts (pinhão)
entries.voxel_shape: straight column topped by upturned symmetrical whorls of branches, like a green candelabra
entries.notes: The candelabra giant of the southern Brazilian highlands; losing the araucaria forest is losing a whole skyline.

entries.name: Palo borracho
entries.leaves: deciduous, compound hands of leaflets, drop in winter
entries.flowers: large pink hibiscus-like blooms on bare branches, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: bulging green bottle trunk armed with woody spines, crown of pink flowers on bare limbs
entries.notes: The 'drunken tree': a green swollen bottle that flowers pink while bare. Spines on the trunk make it awkward to hug.

entries.name: Bunya pine
entries.leaves: evergreen, stiff pointed leaves spiralling around the branches, dome-like crown
entries.flowers: cones; female cones huge, up to 10 kg
entries.fruit: massive round cones dropping heavy bunya nuts
entries.voxel_shape: enormous symmetrical dome on a sheer trunk; Aboriginal feasting grounds gather under it
entries.notes: Tribes walked hundreds of km for the bunya festivals when the great cones dropped; the tree is a calendar you can eat.

entries.name: Yerba mate
entries.leaves: evergreen, glossy dark, thick, picked and dried for mate
entries.voxel_shape: dense dark evergreen with a tidy crown; pruned to head height in the plantations around it
uses: mate (caffeinated infusion drunk through a bombilla)
entries.notes: South America's coffee: a hollowed gourd, a silver straw, and a shared mate passed around the circle. Quintessential social drink.

entries.name: Shiitake
entries.leaves: none (fungus); broad brown cap with white flecks, cracking in dry weather
entries.fruit: cultivated (and wild-growing) on oak and other hardwood logs
entries.voxel_shape: brown umbrella mushroom growing in clusters on fallen oak logs
uses: food (umami staple of East Asian cooking)
entries.notes: Second most cultivated mushroom on Earth; grows on inoculated oak logs. A log-based farm is a very satisfying build.

entries.name: Reishi (lingzhi)
entries.leaves: none (fungus); shiny reddish-brown lacquered shelf bracket, white rim while growing
entries.fruit: shelf brackets on dead hardwood stumps and logs
entries.voxel_shape: glossy kidney-shaped shelf mushroom glued to stumps, lacquer-red with a white edge
entries.notes: The 'mushroom of immortality': almost never eaten directly, steeped or tinctured. Rare in the wild, hoarded in old Chinese art.
